papers.title: Replacing Large Language Models with Jev Decision Models for Low-Latency Edge Service Orchestration
papers.problem: Apps that ask a language model to read each request wait too long, so requests miss their time limit.
papers.fix: A small decision model cut median wait by 22.7-64.5% and kept 0.91-0.95 of requests exact and on time.
papers.practicalUseCase: Language models can be too slow for fixed time limits, so use a small decision model for simple requests.
papers.limitation: It works only for requests with few fields; wide requests are the limit.

papers.title: Ego2Act: Evaluating Goal-Directed Manipulation in Egocentric Video Generation
papers.problem: Video models are tested on single short actions, so nobody knows if they can plan many steps.
papers.fix: Tests on 2,640 videos showed models skip steps, leave later steps without needed states, and fail at fine physical motion.
papers.practicalUseCase: Do not trust video models to simulate multi-step tasks yet, so check each step by hand.
papers.limitation: The test covers only hand tasks in everyday scenes, seen from the first-person view.

papers.title: MemFold: Learning Compact Soft Memory for Long-Context Personalization via On-Policy Optimization
papers.problem: Assistants that serve one user for a long time must track changing preferences, but long text history grows without limit.
papers.fix: MemFold packs memory into fixed-size vectors and scored highest on two long-history tests, winning by more at longer history.
papers.practicalUseCase: Fixed-size memory can beat a growing text history, so consider compact memory for long-running assistants.
papers.limitation: Results come from three Qwen models and benchmark tests, not from real users.

papers.title: Persona Dosing: Calibrated Activation Steering for Graded Trait Control
papers.problem: Steering a language model needs a strength setting, but that setting does not tell you how strongly a trait shows.
papers.fix: PersonaDose raised trait expression by 33.2, 18.3, and 17.8 points over the baseline on three models.
papers.practicalUseCase: You can request a trait level and get close, so test the real output before you ship.
papers.limitation: Calibrated requests reached only 14-22 of 28 targets per model, and coherence dropped for some traits.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks set up sustainability committees, but nobody knew if those committees improve environmental results in Islamic banks.
papers.fix: Committees raised overall environmental scores and resource reduction in Islamic banks, but not green products or innovation.
papers.practicalUseCase: Islamic bank committees may mostly give symbolic results, so check for real green products before you trust a bank.
papers.limitation: The study shows links in emerging markets, not proof that committees cause the changes.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk are growing, but nobody knew what drives the size of each issue.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts, government issuers, and social purposes produced larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Sustainability sukuk stay a tiny market share, so policy should push issuance beyond Indonesia, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia.
papers.limitation: The data stops at 2022 and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan invest in AI and big data, but the effect on results was unclear.
papers.fix: AI use, data analysis skill, and data management all link to better competitiveness and sustainable development in 15 Islamic banks.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks that want an edge should invest in AI and data practice, not only staff digital skills.
papers.limitation: A one-time survey of 214 managers in Jordan shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks need to know what drives their growth, and whether Islamic and conventional banks grow the same way.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries, ICT adoption drove growth most, and high-tech exports helped only when combined with ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Digital tools drive bank growth, so invest in digital infrastructure before anything else.
papers.limitation: Data covers 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, so other regions may differ.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many Muslim-majority countries have little financial inclusion, even though Islamic finance has grown fast.
papers.fix: In 35 countries, income, education, institutions, internet access, population, and age dependency drive inclusion in OIC countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC countries gain most from digital infrastructure and from helping youth and women, so policy should start there.
papers.limitation: The data covers only 35 countries from 2005 to 2021 and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant tests and peer comparison, but nobody had pooled how often they feel like frauds.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings were frequent among medical students worldwide, though results varied widely between studies.
papers.practicalUseCase: Many medical students feel like frauds, so schools should measure it and offer support.
papers.limitation: Study results differed a lot by sampling method and region, so the pooled number is uncertain.

papers.title: Psychometric properties of the Arabic Perceived Digital Well-Being Scale (PDWS) in Saudi young adults
papers.institution: Imam Mohammad ibn Saud Islamic University
papers.problem: Digital well-being studies focus on addiction and risk, and Arabic speakers had no tool to measure the positive side.
papers.fix: The Arabic digital well-being scale showed three clear parts: emotional, social, and cognitive, and linked to life satisfaction.
papers.practicalUseCase: Better feelings about phone use link to higher life satisfaction and less fear of missing out, so track it.
papers.limitation: Only young adults in Riyadh took part, and the design shows links, not cause.
